textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 social-science · From Barter to Money · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Barter means exchanging goods and services directly for other goods and services without using money. A transaction is a piece of business done between people to buy and sell.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Barter means exchanging goods and services directly for other goods and services without using money. A transaction is a piece of business done between people to buy and sell.
beats.speakEn: Barter means exchanging goods and services directly for other goods and services without using money. A transaction is a piece of business done between people to buy and sell.

beats.en: People looked for a common medium of exchange that everybody accepted. For a long time they used commodities such as cowrie shells, salt, tea, tobacco, cloth, cattle, seeds and even feather coils.
beats.speakEn: People looked for a common medium of exchange that everybody accepted. For a long time they used commodities such as cowrie shells, salt, tea, tobacco, cloth, cattle, seeds and even feather coils.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 social-science · From Barter to Money · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Metal coins came next. Because metals last and can be divided and carried, they were ideal. Coins were made of precious metals such as gold, silver and copper or their alloys.

beats.en: Metal coins came next. Because metals last and can be divided and carried, they were ideal. Coins were made of precious metals such as gold, silver and copper or their alloys. An alloy is a mixture of metals.
beats.speakEn: Metal coins came next. Because metals last and can be divided and carried, they were ideal. Coins were made of precious metals such as gold, silver and copper or their alloys. An alloy is a mixture of metals.

beats.en: Metal coins are heavy to carry in large amounts. The search for a more convenient form ended with paper money, first issued in India by banks such as the Bank of Bengal and the Bank of Bombay.
beats.speakEn: Metal coins are heavy to carry in large amounts. The search for a more convenient form ended with paper money, first issued in India by banks such as the Bank of Bengal and the Bank of Bombay.
